Hi Tom - thanks for the spreadsheet. Answers to your telemetry / cookie questions (high level):

1) Telemetry & request data:
- Hosted API: request payloads (prompts) are processed in-memory for inference. By default, we do not persist customer prompts beyond short-lived KV cache used for streaming and model context. Persistent logging of request content is opt-in and only enabled under specific contract terms (we can offer strict data retention or no-retention options for enterprise customers).
- Telemetry: we collect anonymized usage metrics (tokens per request, latency, error rates, route IDs) and feature usage events for the Console. These metrics do not contain customer prompt text.

2) Cookies & third-party trackers:
- Console uses a minimal session cookie for auth (HttpOnly, Secure).
- Product analytics (aggregate only) are captured via a first-party analytics endpoint we host; we do not send console usage to ad networks.
- Docs site uses Google Analytics for public docs and Cloudflare for CDN - both are documented and can be disabled for private deployments.

3) Data residency / subprocessors:
- We offer region-pinned deployments (us/eu) for hosted data; Dedicated and Private modes can be deployed inside customer VPCs.
- Subprocessors list is maintained in our security portal; happy to share the current list under NDA.

If you want, I can produce a one-page tech note that maps each questionnaire row to our answer and call out items needing an NDA. Marissa - I'll draft that and share to this thread.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
